members.note: Against the widget's measured pixel rect. False for a geometry with no viewport position at all -- a render-target canvas, a world-space one with no camera.

Assumes the point lies in the widget's own plane, which is true of every 2D interface. Returns false for a canvas whose scaler cannot be inverted -- world space above all, where the raycaster is the right tool.
Local has its origin at the widget's BOTTOM-left, not Slate's top-left: every other normalized coordinate in this framework already puts zero at the bottom left.
Always zero, because local coordinates are defined from that corner -- the same answer UMG gives for an ordinary widget. Kept so a graph written against UMG reads the same.
Measured from the rect's two projected corners, so a canvas scaler, a render scale and an ancestor's scale are all already in it.
Named for what it transforms rather than with a type prefix. The wider axis decides for a non-uniformly scaled widget, as in UMG.
Per axis, so a non-uniform scale is honoured here where the scalar version has to pick one.

This framework's brush is FDreamUIImageBrush, so the node is named for it. Exact on the floats rather than tolerant: the question a caller asks with == is 'did anybody change this brush', and a near-comparison would answer no to a one-pixel nudge. The node lives on the widget library because the other brush verbs do.
Hands back both the pixel position and the DPI-scaled one, as UMG does.
No bIncludeWindowPosition parameter: a screen position and a viewport pixel position are the same space here, because the framework draws inside the viewport and never against the desktop.
Identity, for the reason on the row above. It exists so a ported graph keeps its shape and so the equivalence is stated somewhere.
